scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Squared-logarithmic randomized k-server on arbitrary metrics” (preprints/Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-on-arbitrary-metrics-September-24-2026/Squared-logarithmic-randomized-k-server-on-arbitrary-metrics-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 110 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 db9f0de04f757cf3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant C < ∞ such that, for every integer k ≥ 2, every metric space (X, d) with at least k + 1 points, and every s ∈ Xk, there exist a randomized online policy A and a finite B ≥ 0 satisfying E costA,s(σ) ≤ C ( log(k + 1) )2 OPTX,d,k,s(σ) + B (1.1) for every finite request sequence σ. The constant C is independent of every property of the metric. The number B may depend on (X, d), k, s, but not on the sequence or its length. The same policy serves all finite sequences and horizons. If the initial positions are distinct, one may take B = 0.
